label: copy phase, length-dependent mid/late position, favours inputs 2/0/g/j/l/i/y
predicate: (phase == 2) & ((L == 3) & (recall_idx == 2) | (((L <= 4) & (recall_idx == 2)) | ((L >= 6) & (recall_idx >= 4) & (recall_idx <= 6)) | ((L == 9) & (recall_idx == 8))) & isin(in_tok, [tok("2"), tok("0"), tok("g"), tok("j"), tok("l"), tok("i"), tok("y")]))
explanation: Active only in the copy phase at recall_idx >= 2 (the bare condition (phase==2)&(recall_idx>=2) gives recall 0.9997 but precision 0.14). It never fires in the original phase, on the delimiter, or at recall_idx 0-1, and only on repeat inputs (in_first=0, which is always true during copy). Firing rate depends on position and length together. It is near-certain at the final step of L=3 sequences (recall_idx 2, precision 0.998), and these give the largest activations (top examples are all L=3 with the second original token fed back, e.g. c 2 m <DEL> c [2]). It is also common at recall_idx 2 for L=4 (0.43), at recall_idx 4-6 for L>=6 (0.15-0.32), and at the last step of L=9. It is nearly silent for L=5 and at recall_idx 2 when L>=5. The input token adds a graded effect: 2, 0, g, j, l, i, y have about 2-4x lift. The positional template alone gets mass recall 0.84 at precision 0.24. Adding the token filter raises precision to 0.59 but drops recall to 0.48, so the gating is clearly incomplete.
